purpose: real-task pilot 2026-10-14, stage B: the predeclared bugfix and feature repeated once per arm in fresh sessions

tasks.taskText: The CSS generator (lib/generator) automatically inserts a space between two adjacent tokens when leaving them adjacent would change how the text tokenizes (for example `1%` followed by `var(` or `#ff0000`). That rule is correct for values the parser turned into nodes, but it is also applied to Raw nodes, whose string value is re-tokenized on output. A raw value is text the parser deliberately left untouched (for example when parsing with `parseValue: false` or `parseRulePrelude: false`), so it must be emitted exactly as written. Today `generate(parse('span#foo { border: 1%var(--a)#ff0000; }', { parseRulePrelude: false, parseValue: false }))` returns `span #foo{border:1% var(--a) #ff0000}`; it must return `span#foo{border:1%var(--a)#ff0000}`. Automatic whitespace must still be inserted where a raw value meets its surroundings (the space in `@media screen` when the prelude is raw must stay) and for fully parsed values: `generate(parse('span#foo { border: 1%var(--a)#ff0000; }'))` must still give `span#foo{border:1% var(--a) #ff0000}`. The change belongs in lib/generator (create.js and its token-before logic). All existing generate, round-trip and source-map tests must keep passing; do not edit tests or fixtures.

chai's `.oneOf(list)` assertion (function oneOf in lib/chai/core/assertions.js) has a `contain`/`include` form that asserts the subject array or string contains at least one member of the list. That form only uses strict identity via indexOf, so the `deep` flag has no effect: expect([[1], [2]]).to.deep.contain.oneOf([[1], [2]]) currently fails with "expected [ [ 1 ], [ 2 ] ] to contain one of [ [ 1 ], [ 2 ] ]". Add deep support to the contain form. When the `deep` flag is set and the subject is an array, a list member counts as contained if any subject element is deep-equal to it (use the same deep-equality utility the file already uses for other deep assertions); without the deep flag the current strict behavior must be unchanged, so expect([[1]]).to.not.contain.oneOf([[1]]) still passes. The failure messages for the contain form must say "deeply" when the deep flag is set: expect([[1]]).to.deep.contain.oneOf([[2]]) must throw "expected [ [ 1 ] ] to deeply contain one of [ [ 2 ] ]" and expect([[1]]).to.not.deep.contain.oneOf([[1]]) must throw "expected [ [ 1 ] ] to not deeply contain one of [ [ 1 ] ]". Nested cases such as expect([[[1]]]).to.deep.contain.oneOf([[[1]]]) must pass. String subjects, the non-contain form of oneOf, the list-must-be-an-array check and all existing messages stay as they are. Do not edit the test directory.
